hypothesis: X2 of the 29 Oct plan (Jerome: 'try other parametric families of kernel on the Laplace case and other cases'). E56 asks whether EM-BP's advantage belongs to the mixture or to the structure on the Laplace chain, which lives in the SHIFT class K(a'|a) = phi(a' - alpha a). E57 asks what happens when the class is right and when it is wrong, on three chains matched to the Laplace chain in variance (1) and lag-one correlation (0.85), so that every linear method sees the same covariance and every difference comes from shape: (i) BIMODAL increment, a' = 0.85 a + eps with eps an equal mixture of two Gaussians (E14b's member, kappa = 0.6, increment excess kurtosis -0.72): in the shift class; (ii) NONLINEAR DRIFT, a' = A tanh(a) + sigma eps: the conditional mean is not linear in a, so no shift kernel contains it (a directed, two-moded cousin of the phi^4 chain); (iii) HETEROSCEDASTIC, a' = 0.85 a + s0 sqrt(1 + c a^2) eps: the conditional scale depends on a, so no shift kernel contains it either. Expectation: inside the class the basis matters little and every kernel beats the networks; outside it the shift families and the mixture lose their edge and only the agnostic kernels (log-linear 2-D, neural energy) keep it.
design: CHAINS (calibrated before any code ran, from the TRUE kernels only: tools/core/calibrate_e57.py, eigenvector of the grid operator on |a| <= 12, 1201 points): bimodal = markov_score.priors.GaussianMixtureAR1(rho=0.85, kappa=0.6); tanh = K(a'|a) = N(a'; A tanh(a), sigma^2) with A = 1.303746, sigma = 0.497509 (Var 1.000000, lag-1 corr 0.850000, stationary law two-moded, excess kurtosis -0.882, mass beyond |a| > 8: 2e-43); hetero = K(a'|a) = N(a'; 0.85 a, s0^2 (1 + c a^2)) with c = 0.25, s0 = 0.471169 (Var 0.9993 and lag-1 corr 0.8499 on the truncated grid, excess kurtosis 2.04, mass beyond |a| > 8: 3.4e-5). Every chain starts from a_1 ~ N(0, 1), the convention of every prior in the package, so the reference BP with the default initial law is exact. The two new chains get a sample() and a log_transition_matrix() in markov_score.priors, tested against the calibration. DATA: E03's protocol with E57's own tags (e57-<chain>-train/val/test and e57-<chain>-em-split/-em-noise): L = 32, the twelve frozen levels, grid 401 on [-8, 8], N in (32, 128, 512, 2048), one noisy view per training chain for the kernel arms, validation 1024 and test 2048 chains per seed. Reference: exact grid BP with each chain's true kernel; the linear floor: the LMMSE of the true covariance on the same test bundle. KERNEL ARMS (EM through exact grid BP, E56's code and settings, checkpoint with the lowest pooled validation BP risk on E55's EM_LADDER to 2400): spline, rbf, fourier, legendre (markov_score.shift_kernel, 25 parameters each); loglinear2d (100); energy (width = E56's screen winner, read from E56_dev/winners.json, no new screen); mixture (markov_score.kernels.MixtureInnovationKernel, C = 8, 25 parameters, E30's start rho 0.3 var 0.8). NETWORK ARMS: global MLP, window CNN, BiGRU, U-Net, each with E03's screened winner configuration (outputs/E03/winners.json; no re-screen), E03's training recipe on the CLEAN training chains (per-example level from the twelve, fresh noise at every step, Adam, checkpoint ladder), checkpoint selected on the validation bundle. KERNEL ERROR as E56: the stationary-weighted Hellinger distance to the true conditional law. ROWS per (chain, seed, N, arm, t) with E56's columns; networks with E03's.

predeclared_predictions.P1: Inside the class (bimodal). Each of the four shift families and the mixture has a lower seed-mean pooled test risk than the best of the four networks (the lowest seed-mean at that N) at every N in (32, 128, 512, 2048), and is lower in at least 7 of 8 paired seeds at each N.
predeclared_predictions.P2: Outside the class, the family matters (tanh and hetero). At N = 2048, the better of the two agnostic arms (lower seed mean) has a lower risk than every shift family and than the mixture, each in at least 7 of 8 paired seeds, on both chains.
predeclared_predictions.P3: Outside the class, the agnostic kernels keep the edge (tanh and hetero). At N in (512, 2048) the better agnostic arm has a lower seed-mean risk than the best network, and is lower in at least 6 of 8 paired seeds, on both chains.
predeclared_predictions.P4: Outside the class, at the level of the kernel. At N = 2048 the better agnostic arm (by seed-mean kernel error) has a lower kernel error than every shift family and the mixture in at least 7 of 8 paired seeds, on both chains.

descriptive.D1: Thesis Fig. 6.3 per chain and family: the learned conditional law K(.|a) at a = -1, 0, 1 against the truth, N = 128, 512, 2048.
descriptive.D2: Do the shift families fall to the linear floor outside the class, as the mixture does on the phi^4 field? Each shift family's seed-mean risk over the linear floor's, per chain and N.
descriptive.D3: The network ranking per chain (which architecture is best where).
descriptive.D4: Seconds per EM iteration per arm and chain.

predeclared_analysis: tools/core/read_e57.py, written with tests/test_read_e57.py in BOTH directions on made-up tables before any confirmatory row exists, on the pattern of read_e56 (a failed or missing fit counts AGAINST every prediction it enters; a seed mean needs all eight seeds; a paired win needs both rows). Gates before any verdict: G1, the reference and every arm of a (chain, seed) were scored on the same test bundle (one hash per (chain, seed, N) within one deployment; kernels and networks of one chain run from one deployment); G2, GEM monotonicity as in E56; G3, failed fits count against; G4, at the cap read from the selected checkpoint (>= 2400) and reported as an upper bound where more than 4 of 8 fits are capped.
